nodes.title: One-step linear equations
nodes.description: Solve equations of the form x + a = b or ax = b using a single inverse operation.
nodes.primer_md:
## One-step equations

An equation says two expressions are equal. To solve `x + a = b` or `ax = b`, undo the single operation with its inverse on **both** sides so the equation stays balanced.

**When to use:** isolate `x` in one move. **Outline:** identify the operation → apply inverse → check by substitution.

nodes.title: Two-step linear equations
nodes.description: Solve ax + b = c with two inverse operations in a deliberate order.
nodes.primer_md:
## Two-step equations

Forms like `ax + b = c` need a deliberate order: undo addition/subtraction first, then undo multiplication/division.

**Why order matters:** clearing the constant first leaves a one-step multiply/divide.

nodes.title: Variables on both sides
nodes.description: Collect like terms when the unknown appears on both sides of a linear equation.
nodes.primer_md:
## Variables on both sides

When `x` appears on both sides, collect variable terms on one side and constants on the other, then finish as a one- or two-step equation.

**Outline:** subtract (or add) a variable term → simplify → isolate `x`.

nodes.title: Linear inequalities
nodes.description: Solve and express simple linear inequalities; flip the inequality when multiplying by a negative.
nodes.primer_md:
## Linear inequalities

Inequalities use `<`, `>`, `≤`, `≥`. Solving steps mirror equations, **except** multiplying or dividing by a negative flips the inequality.

**Check:** pick a test value from your solution set.

nodes.title: Simple quadratics
nodes.description: Solve x^2 = k and (x - h)^2 = k by square roots.
nodes.primer_md:
## Simple quadratics

Equations like `x² = k` or `(x − h)² = k` are solved with square roots. Remember both positive and negative roots when they exist.

**Outline:** isolate the square → take ± square root → solve for `x`.

nodes.title: Combining like terms
nodes.description: Add and subtract like terms to simplify algebraic expressions.
nodes.primer_md:
## Combining like terms

Like terms share the same variable power. Combine coefficients only; unlike terms stay separate.

**Outline:** group like terms → add/subtract coefficients → rewrite cleanly.

nodes.title: Distributive property
nodes.description: Expand a(b+c) and simplify resulting expressions.
nodes.primer_md:
## Distributive property

`a(b + c) = ab + ac`. Expand carefully with signs, then combine like terms if needed.

**Outline:** multiply each term inside → watch negatives → simplify.

nodes.title: Clearing fractions in equations
nodes.description: Multiply through by an LCD to clear denominators before solving.
nodes.primer_md:
## Clearing fractions

Multiply every term by a common denominator to clear fractions, then solve the resulting integer equation.

**Outline:** find LCD → multiply through → solve as usual.

nodes.title: Compound inequalities
nodes.description: Solve chained inequalities a < x < b with consistent operations.
nodes.primer_md:
## Compound inequalities

Forms like `a < x < b` are two inequalities at once. Apply the same operation to all three parts.

**Outline:** treat as a chain → isolate `x` in the middle → graph if useful.

nodes.title: Absolute value equations
nodes.description: Solve |A| = k by splitting into two linear cases.
nodes.primer_md:
## Absolute value equations

`|A| = k` (k ≥ 0) splits into `A = k` or `A = −k`. Solve each case and check extraneous results.

**Outline:** isolate absolute value → split cases → solve → verify.

nodes.title: Difference of squares
nodes.description: Factor a^2 - b^2 and solve related equations.
nodes.primer_md:
## Difference of squares

`a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)`. Factor first when solving equations set to zero.

**Outline:** recognize pattern → factor → zero-product property.

nodes.title: Graphing linear equations
nodes.description: Interpret and plot y = mx + b on the coordinate plane.
nodes.primer_md:
## Graphing linear forms

`y = mx + b` is a line: slope `m`, intercept `b`. Plotting helps check solutions of related equations.

**Outline:** identify slope/intercept → plot two points → connect.
